title: Did you know… breakthrough moments are often preceded by silence?
paragraphs: Did you know… breakthrough moments are often preceded by silence?
Silence.

Not the peaceful kind.
The kind that makes you question if God is even listening.

You prayed.
You cried.
You showed up.
And heaven said… nothing.
But here’s what we miss:
Some of the loudest miracles in Scripture were born in the quietest seasons.

Before the Red Sea split—
there was a trapped nation, hearing only the sound of Pharaoh’s army behind them.

Before Lazarus walked out—
there were four days of unbearable silence in a tomb.

Before the resurrection—
there was a dead Friday… and a silent Saturday.

No voice.
No movement.
No sign.
Just… silence.
And that’s where faith gets real.

Because silence will either make you doubt God—
or drive you deeper into Him.
The truth?

God is never absent in your silence.
He’s working in ways your noise could never understand.
“But I called… and He didn’t answer.”

He did.
Just not with words.

Sometimes His answer is preparation.
Sometimes it’s protection.
Sometimes it’s a breaking before a breakthrough.
And here’s the Gospel:
On the cross, Jesus experienced the ultimate silence.
“My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”

He took the silence of our sin—
so we could receive the voice of grace.

Because of Christ, your silence is not abandonment.
It’s positioning.

Not rejection.
Redirection.

Not the end.
The setup.
So if you’re in that quiet place right now…
Don’t run.
Lean in.

Because breakthrough doesn’t always shout first—
sometimes it whispers through the waiting.

And when God finally moves…
you’ll realize He was never silent at all.
Someone you love is drowning in quiet right now.
Remind them:
God is still speaking—even in the silence.
From silence to breakthrough—because Jesus rewrites everything.
